evidence: Premises hold after full-text search for activation, retirement, resurrection, dormant/unoccupied seats, exclusions, and latest intent across all four reviewed docs. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:18 says closing a live tab retires its seat; :32 says transcript work activates an absent summarizer occupant; :16 says reconcile latest committed intent. DESIGN-NOTES.md:197 distinguishes never-activated absence from retirement; :247 and :258 approve unqualified activation for an unoccupied summarizer, while :250 explicitly leaves the retired/unoccupied boundary unresolved for arbitrary seats. DESIGN-NOTES.md:217 and CURRENT-DESIGN.md:24 protect locally retired template members from recreation, but neither states whether summarizer-triggered activation may override that retirement or must leave durable requests for reassignment/discovery. Thus a deliberately retired summarizer and pending/new transcript processing produce competing instructions without a specified outcome. Narrowing: this is a summarizer-specific lifecycle precedence gap, not a claim that retired seats generally auto-resurrect or that transcript requests are lost.
